data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 conflates a structural property of the log with a semantic property of the writer's operation. The mechanism it describes—tracking which events have been appended and suppressing late-arriving duplicate retries—IS standard idempotence (deduplication). The ordering of non-duplicate writes is preserved by the append-only medium itself, not by any additional property of the writer's append operation. The writer needs idempotence ('don't append a duplicate'); the ordering of surviving events is an inherent consequence of 'append-only,' not a separate, stronger requirement imposed on the writer. Claiming the log requires a property 'strictly stronger than RFC 9110 idempotence' of its writers is a category error: it merges log structure with operation semantics. The causal chain it offers (dedup via sequence numbers) is exactly the causal chain of idempotence, not of a distinct stronger property. Additionally, SRC_001 largely fails to address the problem's first ask—'what precisely distinguishes an idempotent operation from a safe one'—since it never defines 'safe' or articulates the safe-vs-idempotent distinction.
